text:
ashley: dropping an nsys capture from the latest nightly that shows a weird shift in hot kernels after the prefetch change (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/428)
ashley: overall tail latency spiked ~18% on a 2k token run, and the kernel time breakdown points to a new top-3 offender: kv_prefetch_worker
ashley: quick table from the trace (top kernels by GPU time):\n```\n1  kv_prefetch_worker            32.4%  (old: 2.1%)\n2  attention_fwd_fused           18.7%\n3  matmul_batched               12.3%\n4  softmax_reduce               8.9%\n5  kv_lookup_coalesce           5.1%\n6  layernorm_bwd                3.2%\n```\nashley: note the huge jump for kv_prefetch_worker — likely due to the new aggressive prefetch depth + continuous-batching interaction
miguel: ugh, I was the one who landed the prefetch depth change (commit abc1234). I can repro locally with nsys as well. My runs show lots of launch overheads and repeated memcpys between host<>device around the prefetcher
jordan: can you paste the nvprof/nvtx snippet? want to see if it overlaps with the KV cache writes or it's a separate kernel wave
ashley: nvtx ranges look like this in the capture: `|batch_dispatch| -> |kv_prefetch| -> |kv_writeback|` repeated per micro-batch, which suggests prefetcher is doing synchronous IO per micro-batch instead of issuing async device ops
ashley: command used: `nsys profile --trace=nvtx,cuda --output=/tmp/capture -t 30s --capture-range=nvtx`\n
ashley: logs show memcpy kind=HtoD 3.2GB total over 30s and many small memcpys (~1-2MB) instead of batched transfers
devon: that pattern screams batching heuristic regression. The change reduced batch coalescing threshold from 8->4, right? small batches trigger more prefetch rounds
miguel: yes, I lowered the coalescing threshold hoping to reduce latency for short sequences. But didn't consider interaction with prefetch depth which multiplies memcpy ops
jordan: two quick mitigation options: 1) bump coalescing threshold back and add a debounce so prefetcher aggregates HtoD; 2) make kv_prefetch_worker use cudaMemcpyAsync + better stream affinity and pipeline with kernel launches
ashley: tried option 2 in a quick fork: switching to async and reusing a pinned buffer reduced memcopy stalls, nvtx shows kv_prefetch down from 32% -> 9% and tail latency back to baseline on my box
perf-bot: perf alert: regression detected in nightly 2026-03-17 03:12 UTC — latency +18% relative to baseline; traces attached to ticket #INF-622
miguel: thanks — I'll open a revert PR for the coalescing change and push the async prefetch patch as a follow-up (won't land both in same deploy)
devon: before revert, can we try a canary with async prefetch + coalescing at 6? small rollout on dedicated pool would prove it's safe
ashley: +1 to canary. also want to add a perfetto capture for longer tail behavior and a flamegraph export process so ranking is automated next time
jordan: I'll add a quick analyzer to the trace pipeline to flag sudden new hotspots (delta > 10% of total GPU time) and create an ephemeral alert in the console
miguel: plan: (1) open revert PR for coalescing threshold, (2) push async prefetch patch to feature branch, (3) run canary on dedicated-2 pool, (4) collect nsys + perfetto + failure repro cases, (5) re-evaluate rollout. ETA: today EOD
devon: lmk if you want me to run canary; I can schedule a 30-min window and capture perfetto export
ashley: tagging the trace link: https://artifacts.internal/redwood/nsys/3509876543/capture.qdrep and the ticket INF-622
miguel: thanks all. will update the thread with PR links. brief note: watch for SM occupancy drop during kv_prefetch spikes — if occupancy falls <40% during those windows that's another indicator the prefetcher is serializing the compute
ashley: confirmed occupancy dips to 28% during kv_prefetch bursts in the trace — another smoking gun\nashley: closing loop: async + pinned buffer fix + cautious coalescing bump seems to return perf to expected. we'll iterate on kernel selection heuristics separately (priority: reduce prefetch worker invocation rate and prefer batched HtoD)
